video_title: Are the Pacers Sleepers? Rick Carlisle on Indiana, Coaching Luka Dončić & Playing With Larry Bird

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on Draymond Green's defensive impact and legacy
quotes.excerpt: Draymond Green has built one of the most impactful defensive careers in NBA history.
quotes.quote: Draymond Green has built one of the most impactful defensive careers in NBA history. Although his scoring has never been elite, his versatility, leadership, passing, and defensive intelligence have been central to the Golden State Warriors dynasty. Drafted 35th overall in the second round by the Warriors in 2012, four-time NBA champion, four-time NBA All-Star, 2016-17 Defensive Player of the Year, widely regarded as one of the greatest defensive seasons ever by a forward, nine-time NBA All-Defensive team selection, two-time All-NBA selection, two-time Olympic gold medalist. Green revolutionized the small-ball center role at 6-6. He routinely guarded all five positions while serving as a Warriors defensive quarterback and one of the NBA's best playmakers from the frontcourt. His chemistry with Steph Curry has been a defining feature of Golden State's offense and defense.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on his coaching start with the Detroit Pistons
quotes.excerpt: I owe a lot to Joe Dumars, he was the guy that gave me my first opportunity.
quotes.quote: I owe a lot to Joe Dumars, he was the guy that gave me my first opportunity as an NBA head coach. We took over a 32-win team. I remember at the press conference, I was asked about what expectations should be and do you think it's possible to be a .500 team. My response was, why would we want to put a mediocre number like 41 wins on something and set the expectations lower? Rather than putting a number on it, let's commit to a process and see where we can go with this thing. We don't want to put a cap on what we believe we might be capable of. I had a great defensive coach in Mike Curry, and we had three elite defenders in Ben Wallace, Cliff Robinson, and Mike Curry in that first year. We got to the second round of the playoffs and we won 50 games.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the impact of trading for Rasheed Wallace
quotes.excerpt: They traded for Rasheed Wallace and that changed everything because he was a guy of your ilk.
quotes.quote: They traded for Rasheed Wallace and that changed everything because he was a guy of your ilk as a defender. He was a traffic cop. They were a team that didn't necessarily have a set defensive system, but they were so smart and with his versatility and Ben Wallace, they were constantly changing coverages, so you didn't know exactly what was going on. As I've watched you guys over the years, I see you doing the same thing. It's maddening as a coach because as you try to prepare your team, you have a guy like you who can switch, who can blitz, who is basically running the show almost like a defensive coordinator, and it makes it very, very difficult.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the challenges of being a first-time head coach
quotes.excerpt: When a guy hires a first-time head coach, he's putting his neck out there.
quotes.quote: When a guy hires a first-time head coach, he's putting his neck out there. Joe believed in me and I really appreciated that. And he was a first-time general manager. He was a first-time president and he was making a lot of important decisions. We had a great owner with Mr. Davidson, but he was tough and he was a guy that believed in setting expectations high, so there was a lot going on there. They had a great run. They won that championship in 04. You got to give them their due. I think they went to the finals two or three years in a row after that and they had quite a run there.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on building a successful team in Indiana
quotes.excerpt: The following year, we acquired Stephen Jackson to go along with Reggie Miller, Jermaine O'Neal, Tinsley.
quotes.quote: The following year, we acquired Stephen Jackson to go along with Reggie Miller, Jermaine O'Neal, Tinsley, and that whole group, and we had good depth and we had real talent. It's a dynamic business and things change quickly. They decided to go a different direction and I had to hope that the track record that I had put together to that point, 100 wins in two years and three playoff wins, was going to mean something. And then after a few months, I ended up in Indiana. We had dominated the Pistons my first year in Indiana, which was the year right after my two years in Detroit, and then I think we beat them three times out of three and then they traded for Rasheed Wallace and that changed everything.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the 2004 Pacers-Pistons playoff series
quotes.excerpt: At the end of game six, Paul Pierce gets ejected and we're going into overtime.
quotes.quote: At the end of game six, Paul Pierce gets ejected and we're going into overtime, and they don't have Paul Pierce and we end up losing at home. So we go to game seven in Boston and everybody thinks we're going to get blown out. We end up winning that game by 28 points and that sets up the rematch with the Pistons who we had the brawl with earlier in the year. There was a lot to do about that series, but in the end, it was one of the most resilient performances by an organization and a franchise to overcome that situation, get to the playoffs, win in the playoffs, get to the second round, and then Reggie Miller, he bowed out in his career during that series and he had one of the best runs in those six games against Detroit to end a very dignified career and ultimately a Hall of Fame career.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the 2011 Mavericks championship run
quotes.excerpt: In 2011, it was either now or never. The team was aging.
quotes.quote: In 2011, it was either now or never. The team was aging. The veterans were still at in a part of their prime. Jason Terry was still great, Dirk was great, Jason Kidd was 37 and he was still playing at a very high level. He almost won the MVP a few years earlier with the Nets. I mean, the Nets were an autumn feeder and the Jason Kidd got traded to New Jersey and they had them in the finals twice, you know, so that he still could have that kind of impact. We traded for Tyson Chandler who gave us a defensive guy similar to yourself, very energetic, very vocal, very positive, very upbeat, totally only into winning, and Shawn Marion was a very underrated player. You can make a case that Shawn Marion could be in a conversation for Hall of Fame on a many multiple year, all-star type thing, championship player, great two-way player. He had an unconventional game, but he was an original in his purest form. It was clear to us heading into that final series that we had to have a very simple plan and a big part of it was going to have to be persistence.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the Mavericks' defensive strategy against LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: One of them was a picture from the finals where Jason Kidd was picking up full court.
quotes.quote: One of them was a picture from the finals where Jason Kidd was picking up full court against LeBron James. So we were going to be full court, we were going to make nothing easy and we were going to be persistent. We were always going to be there. We had a zone defense which we had developed really during the previous summer to prepare for that season and Tim Grgurich was a big part of that. Now, Grg came on board with us that year. You know Grg well and Grg is a guy who's really to me the godfather of modern player development and he's just a charismatic figure on a coaching staff. And so we knew our zone was going to have to give us some help in that series because the matchups just weren't there. We had Peja Stojakovic who had played well in the previous series against the Lakers, but the matchups were very difficult against Miami and so the zone, the zone had to help us there.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the Mavericks' intuitive, unpredictable offensive style
quotes.excerpt: You guys have developed a style where you have set plays and you have set options.
quotes.quote: You guys have developed a style where you have set plays and you have set options and stuff like that, but you guys play an intuitive random style, which I think is the hardest style to defend because you don't know what's about to happen. And then offensively, I also think that there's a great deal of merit to that for an offensive standpoint because when you have unpredictability offensively, players can be much more in a reactive mode. And so look, we were going to be in attack mode, we were going to play fast, play random for great opportunities, we were going to count it up later. We were going to gun up the makes and misses later, but every time you got a good look at the basket, you're aggressive and you are attacking.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the musical influences on his coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: I've been influenced by a lot of things and one of the things that's influenced me a lot is music.
quotes.quote: I've been influenced by a lot of things and one of the things that's influenced me a lot is music and I'm a big fan of traditional jazz and trio jazz where there's an unpredictability to how music is played and I was always drawn to that and I think people that watch the game are drawn to the style that you guys play. They're drawn to the style that we play in Indiana because it's random, it's pure, it's player-driven, it's player-empowered. It's hard to guard. I've been fortunate, I've gotten to know some of the great musicians in history, guys like Bruce Hornsby, Christian McBride, Branford Marsalis, Jerry Garcia among others and these guys have influenced me from a basketball standpoint which has been really cool.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the importance of health and conditioning
quotes.excerpt: The big thing this summer is health, getting everybody completely healthy and then ramping up conditioning.
quotes.quote: The big thing this summer is health, getting everybody completely healthy and then ramping up conditioning the way we need to do it so that we can have a healthy training camp and get into the season. Both both years 24 and 25, we went to the conference finals in 24 and we went to the NBA finals game seven in 25, we had slow starts and you know, we want to start fast and finish strong, but I think the whole league is hard. I think the East and the West are going to be, you know, it's apples and orange and I don't know how you can say one is stronger than the other.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on Luka Dončić's development as a player
quotes.excerpt: He was having trouble shooting threes and they were just long shots.
quotes.quote: He was having trouble shooting threes and they were just long shots and he was getting to the mid-range, but he wasn't driving the ball and we said, hey, you need to drive it, you need to be able to shoot threes and he came back in the fall and he was driving it and he was making threes and so his rookie year was pretty damn good and his second year was even better. When Luka came, he came in the fall and the first day of pickup games, he's playing and we have, you know, we have a pretty good veteran team. We had DeAndre Jordan, we had Wes Matthews, we had Harrison Barnes who won a championship with you and some other really good players and Luka's playing with these guys and he is playing like Magic Johnson. He is rebounding and he is throwing dimes like all over the place. He wasn't really even looking to score and I'm like, guys, this guy's like a Magic Johnson type player.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the 2011 Mavericks' offensive strategy
quotes.excerpt: They did this thing in game two of the finals where they ran a 77.
quotes.quote: They did this thing in game two of the finals where they ran a 77, which is a double ball screen and Dirk would roll in the first one and then Tyson Chandler would come and pin down for him and no one had ever seen that action and our guys invented it during the game. Invented it during the fourth quarter of the game and that that was what really triggered our comeback in game two and if we hadn't had the comeback in game two, we're down 15 with six minutes to go and we win that game and then, you know, now it's a five-game series. And so, look, player empowerment is so key when you have a veteran team like those those Mavericks, like your Warriors, you know, and you got a coach like Steve that's, you know, that trusts you guys. I mean, it's it's a powerful situation that can never be duplicated.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the 2006 Mavericks' playoff run
quotes.excerpt: They had Shaq, they had Kobe, you know, they had Lamar Odom who was their sixth man.
quotes.quote: They had Shaq, they had Kobe, you know, they had Lamar Odom who was their sixth man. They had Bynum, they had they had unbelievable size and then, you know, they had Gasol at one time and they had guards that could shoot the ball and look, Fisher was a great player and like Fisher won't won't make the Hall of Fame, but he's a Hall of Fame system player. I mean, you look at what he did in that system and you look at when he had that group of player that kind of a group of players and if they if they if they if they have a belief in the system, I mean, it's it's a powerful situation that can never be duplicated.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the importance of full-court pressure in modern basketball
quotes.excerpt: that system could cause today's teams a lot of problems because they really dictate tempo
quotes.quote: That system could cause today's teams a lot of problems because they really dictate tempo. In our two successful years before this past year where we were all banged up, in order to keep the game fast, we had to go to full-court pickup. It was the only way to keep playoff games fast. Teams didn't want to play as fast as us, and it's grueling. If you think back, and I've had conversations with Phil about this, Phil believed that to play four guards, two starters, two guys off the bench, and to apply full-court pressure in dead-ball situations, in free-throw situations, to always have leverage and friction in the game, was another element of their success.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle's evaluation of Magic Johnson and Larry Bird's greatness
quotes.excerpt: nobody can tell me that Magic Johnson and Larry Bird wouldn't have been in the top players
quotes.quote: Nobody can tell me that Magic Johnson and Larry Bird wouldn't have been in the top players in the league today. Greatness is going to be great regardless of the era. You are going to try to tell me that Russell wouldn't be great in this era? Russell, the guy who threw up before every game because he couldn't stomach the idea of losing and he had such impact on winning, can you imagine having that guy leading your team? That was the early version of Draymond Green.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on Larry Bird's competitive nature and mind games
quotes.excerpt: I've heard some things about Larry Bird, the shit talking, the mind games he played
quotes.quote: I've heard some things about Larry Bird, the shit talking, the mind games he played, all these different things that obviously you can't just pick up on YouTube. Talk to me about Larry Bird, like the type of player, competitor he was, the mind games that he played.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on Larry Bird's humble background and competitive drive
quotes.excerpt: he's a humble guy, but he's a killer competitor and he's a believer that the only thing that matters
quotes.quote: He's from a modest background to say the least. He's a humble guy, but he's a killer competitor and he's a believer that the only thing that matters is winning. Magic Johnson is a believer that the only thing that matters is winning. Larry would sometimes get bored. He was so much better than everybody else during that period. Three years in a row he's MVP in the 80s. He's the best player on the planet for three years plus. There were times when he would just come down, one time he comes down in the break and pulls up and shoots a left-handed jumper from 16 feet on the break and he makes it. I was at dinner a few nights later and I said, 'Larry, when you do something like that, what are you thinking?' He goes, 'I have absolutely no idea. I just do it. Things just happen.'

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the intense rivalry between 80s NBA stars
quotes.excerpt: these guys were bitter rivals and the level of respect was so high
quotes.quote: I see Instagram things all the time about guys that were the baddest MFs back in that day talking about how great he was and that he was the greatest, like Dominique and Worthy and who else, John Salley, I mean, even Isaiah Thomas. These guys were bitter rivals and the level of respect was so high. The mind games, like the stuff with the All-Star game, walking in saying who's coming in second, I mean, come on.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the competitive dynamic between Larry Bird and Danny Ainge
quotes.excerpt: Danny and Larry were always going back and forth in Boston about who the better three-point shooter was
quotes.quote: Danny and Larry were always going back and forth in Boston about who the better three-point shooter was. One time we're getting on the bus like right after the All-Star game, Larry had won it for the first time and he goes, 'Danny.' And Danny goes, 'Yeah, Larry?' He goes, 'Who's the three-point king?' Danny goes, 'You are.' He goes, 'That's right.'

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the intense practices of the 80s Celtics
quotes.excerpt: the year we got Walton, the practices between the starters and the second unit were bloodbaths
quotes.quote: The year we got Walton, the practices between the starters and the second unit were bloodbaths because we were putting on the wall who was winning every day and we beat those guys a lot of days because we were more into it than they were. They were all a bunch of Hall of Famers, but we were finally able to extend leads or erase deficits because Walton was so great. We just give him the ball and just start running around.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on Luka Dončić's competitive nature
quotes.excerpt: Luka's got a lot of that. He has fun with the game, he talks shit
quotes.quote: Luka's got a lot of that. He has fun with the game, he talks shit, you know, he's brash, all that kind of stuff. Larry did it a little more under his breath at times. Other times he stepped up, he got in fights and other stuff like that. As a competitor, I put him up there with Jordan and all the greatest guys.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green on his lifelong fascination with airplanes
quotes.excerpt: I have a fascination with airplanes. Since I was a kid, the first time I ever got
quotes.quote: I have a fascination with airplanes. Since I was a kid, the first time I ever got on an airplane I was 13 years old. If I was ever by the airport or even in my neighborhood, if an airplane would fly over, I would just watch the airplane until I couldn't see it anymore. I've had, and even to this day, when I get on an airplane still, I'm like fascinated by it. I thought it was something that I would outgrow. I never outgrew it. However, I don't know that I trust myself enough to be a pilot, but I love airplanes.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on learning to fly and his aviation experience
quotes.excerpt: I decided if I was going to learn, the best way to do it was to buy a plane.
quotes.quote: I decided if I was going to learn, the best way to do it and leverage it was to buy a plane and then learn how to fly it. So I did that and it was great. My relationships in aviation have been transcended. I've got about 700 hours of both SR, which is prop plane, and jet hours, because Cirrus now makes a single-engine jet.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle caddying for Peter Jacobson at the British Open
quotes.excerpt: Would you have any interest in caddying for me at the British Open?
quotes.quote: I became an assistant out in Portland with the Blazers for PJ Carlesimo. Peter Jacobson, the tour pro who had a very successful career on tour, lived in Portland and I ended up playing with him a couple times. So the second year I was in Portland, we were going to go on a golf trip to Scotland. I get a call from Peter saying, 'Hey look, I don't think Fluff is going to go over there.' Fluff was his caddy. Fluff was the guy that carried for Tiger his first couple three years. He goes, 'Would you have any interest in caddying for me at the British Open?' I'm like, 'What? Are you serious?' He goes, 'Oh yeah, no, I'm serious. You're a competitive guy.' I said, 'Yeah, I mean, make sure you're okay with this.' And so we decided to do it.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle's experience caddying at Lytham & St. Annes
quotes.excerpt: Amazing experience in Scotland, go down to Lytham & St. Annes.
quotes.quote: I went over there, we played Turnberry a few times, we played Prestwick, we played Troon. Amazing experience in Scotland, go down to Lytham & St. Annes. I mean, luckily it was 80 degrees and 5 mile an hour winds and sunshine the whole week. I'm just carrying the bag, there's no gear, no umbrella. It was pretty good.

quotes.speaker: Rick Carlisle
quotes.summary_phrase: Rick Carlisle on the importance of wedge distance in golf
quotes.excerpt: you want to go from being a nine to a six or a five, on those par fives
quotes.quote: Peter told me, 'Look, you want to go from being a nine to a six or a five, on those par fives where you're just winding up trying to hit the green, figure out what your wedge distance is and get great with a wedge and play to your wedge distance, whether it's 90, 80, 100 yards, whatever, and really work on wedge and putter.'
